what_happened: The operator ran job 4kgd directly, ahead of Athena's plan. The job makes interrupted jobs retryable and lets the queue drain pick them up. The reason given was a rescue. Four container restarts in about 22 hours each killed or stalled a running job. Each time the operator had to close the job by hand and ask for it again, because an interrupted job cannot be retried.
cause: The plan ranks work by default type and position. It does not weigh live failure pressure, such as a gap that has already cost four manual rescues, or the owner's priorities. Nothing counts how often an operator has repeated the same manual workaround and raises the job that would remove it. The queue has no priority support, so the operator's only lever is to bypass the plan. The interrupted-job gap was already known: the class for untracked runs killed by container reclaim is in the registry. It was logged but not scheduled as a fix, so each restart cost another manual close and re-ask.
prevention: Make planning use recurrence of operator interventions as an input. When the same gap has produced N or more hand rescues (for example 3), or when the owner marks a priority, the job that fixes the gap moves to the front of the plan automatically. Add queue priority support so the plan can enforce that order without the operator bypassing it. Also give interrupted jobs a retryable state that the drain picks up. That removes this specific rescue.
proposed_request: Change Athena's planner so that open gaps and operator interventions raise a job's rank. If a gap has caused three or more logged manual rescues or overrides, the job that fixes it must be placed ahead of default-ordered work in the plan. The owner's stated priorities must also take precedence over default rung order. Add priority support to the queue so the drain follows the plan's order. Show the reason for each reorder in the plan output. Acceptance: with a test plan containing a gap with three logged interventions, the fixing job is ranked first, and the drain runs it first. A priority set by the owner overrides default order. A plan with no recurring gaps and no owner priority keeps its current order.
